title: One month building Beyond the Rhine: a medieval siege city builder set on the Rhine in 1400, with Claude, Godot & Suno
author: sharbelito
selftext:
Beyond the Rhine is a medieval city builder and siege game set along the Rhine around the year 1400. You start with an empty field, build a town, look after the people who live and work in it, then defend it against sieges with cannons, trebuchets and great crossbows and more. I wanted it to look realistic rather than cartoonish, closer to Manor Lords than to a mobile game. Here’s where it stands after a month of work.

I used Claude for all the code and Suno for the music. Every 3D model comes from human artists (Sketchfab, Quaternius, Mixamo animations), not AI generators, and each one is credited in the game. It started as a single Three.js page which was intended for android, which i coded myself from scratch (and i have an apk for it) and now runs on Godot, with Windows and Android builds from the same project. A few things I did processwise:

* Engine switch: once the Three.js version got too heavy, I ported it to Godot and moved the land generator and the other heavy parts into a C++ module.
* Before thinking about Steam, I checked every model, sound and music track for commercial use. That meant cutting over 600 sound clips taken from a Mount & Blade mod, and every model with a non-commercial licence, then replacing them.
* Historical accuracy: soldier names, towns and events have to fit the year 1400. (yes yes even cannons)
* Fresh land every game: each new game generates a new landscape with the Rhine running through it, and towns are laid out with walls, gates, streets and wards.
* A build after every test round: Windows and Android, so I can test each feature on PC as soon as it’s added.

Gameplay is on my YouTube channel, Beyond the Rhine, and the game is heading to Steam. I’d love feedback, harsh feedback especially, so I know what to fix before release.
